title: Weekend sprint notebook — KPI check-in
content:
Sprint anchor (Feb 20–26)

Purpose: fast personal check-in + micro experiments that can move a single KR this week. Keep it readable — 30–60m to scan.

Top-level goal (Q1 personal OKR tie-in): Reduce unit inference cost while holding 95th perc latency under 200ms for our internal test workload.

Key results I’m tracking this sprint (quantify where possible):
- KR1: Bring per-1k-token cost down 8% from baseline (baseline = $0.78/1k tokens). Target this week: identify 2 opportunities (cache, batch sizing).
- KR2: Reduce cold-start rate for small models from 12% -> 6% for requests under 512 tokens.
- KR3: Add 1 reliable prompt eval that catches a regression before rollout.

Signals to watch (morning checklist):
- Daily throughput: target 18k requests/day (current: 16.9k)
- Median latency (prod-sim): target < 110ms (current: 125ms)
- KV-cache hit rate: baseline 36% -> goal 44%
- Cold-start ratio: baseline 12% -> goal 6%
- Cost delta: run cost dashboard and note % change vs. baseline

This week’s micro-experiments (concrete, one-variable changes):
1) Batch-size tuning on model-small-a: run A/B with batch target 8 vs 12 for 48h. Track median/95th latency and tokens/sec. Hypothesis: 12 will reduce per-token cost ~4% without >10% 95th latency regression. Acceptance: cost drop >=3% and 95th latency increase <=6%.

2) Prefix caching toggle: enable nginx-level sticky header for 40% of traffic -> observe KV-cache hit-rate lift. Hypothesis: sticky headers will increase prefix reuse. Acceptance: KV-cache hit rate +6pp and cold-start ratio -3pp. Rollback criteria: error rate >0.5% or P50 latency + >20ms consistently.

3) Lightweight eval harness: add a small prompt set (25 examples) to CI that runs on PRs touching compilation/kernels. Hypothesis: catches subtle numeric divergence from quantization changes. Acceptance: at least 1 mismatch flagged when we known-broken branch merged in trial.

Quick data snapshot (pulled 2026-03-10 09:30 PST):
- Throughput (24h): 17.2k reqs
- Median latency (prod-sim): 118ms
- P95 latency: 204ms
- KV-cache hit: 38%
- Cold-start ratio: 11.3%
- Estimated per-1k-token cost (rolling): $0.76 (down 2.6% vs 2 weeks ago)

Notes / Observations:
- The P95 spike around 03/08 correlated with a config change to autoscaler cooldown; SRE rolled it back. Need to add a small synthetic test for cooldown logic.
- Priya's batching optimizer PR reduced CPU overhead in the 2-4 token-per-request tail. Worth running a targeted batch-size grid on the small model.

Immediate actions (today):
- Kick off batch-size A/B job (Eliot + me) and add graph to the experiment dashboard (action: create JIRA-3421-A)
- Add 25-case prompt eval to runtime CI (owner: Noel). Quick wins: include a few degenerate quantization cases.
- Schedule 30m sync with Priya to review sticky header plan (proposed: Thu 11am).

Retrospective (mini, for the previous sprint):
- What went well:
  - Faster instrumentation: cost-by-route landed and already surfaced 3 heavy routes.
  - Good cross-team sync: SRE debugged autoscaler with minimal churn.
- What didn’t:
  - I didn't ship the lightweight eval in time; blocked on infra quota for ephemeral workers.
  - Measurement noise: we still have noisy P95 signals when traffic bursts hit; need to aggregate over multiple windows.

Lessons / Ideas:
- Ship smaller eval harnesses earlier — acceptance criteria can be reduced to smoke tests initially.
- Introduce a 5m synthetic probe that exercises the autoscaler path to detect cooldown regressions.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the sticky-header approach safe for multi-tenant customers who have session routing policies? (Ask Solutions Eng.)
- Can we get ephemeral worker quota bumped for personal CI runs? (Talk to infra quota owners.)

Backlog (short):
- [ ] Add synthetic autoscaler probe (owner: Noel)
- [ ] Run batch-size grid for 3 candidate small models (owner: Noel + Eliot)
- [ ] Merge Priya’s batching optimizer and monitor (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Land 25-case eval in CI and enable on release branches (owner: Noel)

Personal notes (voice):
- Keep the week lean — prioritize actions that can produce measurable delta on one KR. I get distracted by “make this perfect” and it delays the signal.
- If an experiment shows a small win, codify it quickly (playbook entry) so we can repeat on other models.

Planned micro-check (end of week):
- Write 3 bullets for each KR: what moved, why, next step. Put in team channel + personal notes.

References / helpful links:
- cost dashboards — /conf/cost-views (CONFLUENCE-2984)
- running-batches playbook — github.com/redwood-inference/ops/playbooks#batching

End of sprint note: keep this doc lightweight, archive once the KR’s primary lift is validated.
